A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same RegionReasoner paper, with complete main text and Appendices A–I. Text extraction and visual comparison support reliable comparison of the equations, tables, figures, and image-embedded dialogue.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection and segmentation experiments, component ablations, qualitative trajectories, V* evaluation, and reward-weight sensitivity results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–4 and 9–11, and revises the qualitative comparison in Figure 2.

M1.justification: The backbone, structured outputs, reference-citation and global–local consistency rewards, inference procedure, and training formulation in Section 4 are unchanged. Revised example outputs do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same RefCOCO+/RefCOCOg multi-round and single-round tasks and V* evaluation. The qualitative scenes are retained; correcting the name MRVR-Bench to RegionDial-Bench does not change dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–2 and 9–10 and Figure 2. VisionReasoner remains the qualitative comparator despite revisions to its displayed outputs.

E3.justification: Splits, dialogue construction, metrics, training settings, and evaluation prompts remain unchanged. Figure 2's revised description of blue ground-truth boxes corrects the display legend; the stated protocol still propagates model predictions during testing.

E4.justification: Figure 2 revises the existing three-turn failure case by replacing VisionReasoner's duplicated later-turn explanations and changing its displayed predictions. The component ablations, reward-weight sensitivity study, and other qualitative cases retain their analytical content.

E5.justification: The fixed-random-seed statement is retained. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests, or other uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Figure 2 changes VisionReasoner's highlighted target from the right-side man to the woman in purple at R2, and from the R1 man to the right-side man at R3, with corresponding revised traces. The later-turn failure pattern remains. All quantitative table entries are unchanged.

T1.justification: The problem definitions, policy and memory equations, reward definitions, and optimization derivations in Sections 3–4 are unchanged. No formal assumptions, proofs, or mathematical properties are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: RegionDial-Bench, reference-grounded reasoning, consistency rewards, and improved multi-round grounding, especially at later turns.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning semantic drift, reference propagation, error accumulation, and external generalization are retained. Appendix I's limitations are unchanged, and Figure 2's caption retains its explanation of the baseline's failures.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hardware and training time, instruction schemas, code link, and promised reproducibility resources are unchanged. The benchmark-name correction in the reproducibility statement does not alter access or technical instructions.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and reference list are unchanged, including the positioning relative to VisionReasoner and SegLLM. No cited work or substantive novelty comparison is added or removed.

P1.justification: v2 replaces two lingering MRVR-Bench references with RegionDial-Bench in the ethics and reproducibility statements and revises Figure 2's caption and selected dialogue text. The main narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is reformatted, adds correctness checkmarks/crosses, and corrects the legend to identify green detection boxes and red segmentation masks. Figures 1 and 6 receive speech-bubble graphical edits, and text reflows across pages 9–10. Tables and other figures retain their layouts.

improvement.justification: v2 makes Figure 2 easier to assess by correcting its legend and replacing duplicated, mismatched baseline explanations with turn-specific traces aligned to the displayed predictions. Benchmark naming is also more consistent. The benefit is limited: quantitative evidence is unchanged, and the caption still says VisionReasoner lacks explicit citation although its revised R2 trace quotes the reference coordinates.
